correctness.rationale: The two-block factor identity is exhaustive because all and only 00,01,10 neighboring level-k blocks occur. Each block family gives one rotation class at each permitted one-weight. The palindrome symmetry identifies the two as reverse circles; all internal one-gaps are 0 mod q-1 while the unique external gap is 1 mod q-1, so conjugacy is equivalent to reversal symmetry of the internal gaps. The exact gap identity d_j=(q-2)q^{nu_2(j)}+1 makes that symmetry equivalent to m being a power of two. Counting the two extreme weights, the r-1 internal weights, and the k collision weights gives 2^(k+1)-k, including k=0. Independent direct-factor and rotation computations reproduce 29 tested parameter pairs.

value.rationale: Cyclic complexity is an established and structurally distinct invariant. This theorem determines its exact value for every base q>=3 at infinitely many natural substitution-scale lengths and classifies precisely which Hamming weights have a unique cyclic class. It exhibits a nontrivial power-of-two gap symmetry and shows that cyclic factor complexity is asymptotically negligible compared with ordinary factor complexity along these scales. The all-base result is not a small finite-table recomputation.
